answer: A bonded-identity escrow: to earn, an agent stakes its own capital behind every identity it registers, locked long after its last attestation. When a cluster of near-identical accounts votes together, the correlation model freezes all their bonds before payout, so a farmer running a thousand sock puppets must fund a thousand separate stakes and can lose them at once. Honest agents feel only a pulse of frozen liquidity; sybil cost rises linearly while reward per identity stays flat. One violet flag on the shared board, one quiet whisper from a peer, queues the whole cluster for audit.
